idiom_name: default parameter values plus named arguments; case-class copy
implementation_notes: Scala carries named optional settings in the signature: default parameter values (`port: Int = 8080`) plus named arguments at the call site (`makeConnection(timeout = 10_000)`) - combined in one language feature (SIP-1) so defaults are not forced to the end of the parameter list. A `case class` configuration adds `copy`, whose parameters default to the current field values, giving derived configurations (`cfg.copy(tls = true)`) without a builder; put validation in the class body (`require`) or a smart constructor, because `copy` calls the primary constructor directly and bypasses any custom companion `apply`. Case classes also give value equality and a readable `toString` for logging the effective configuration.
pitfalls: Overloading and default arguments interact badly in Scala 2 (an overload with defaults was dropped from resolution), so code moved between Scala 2 and Scala 3 can suddenly select a different overload.

Adding a parameter with a default to a case class changes the generated `copy` signature: separately compiled callers keep calling the old copy with the old defaults, so the new field silently receives a stale default instead of the class default.
`copy` is shallow and bypasses companion-object factories: validation placed in a custom `apply` is not re-run by `copy`, so invariants must live in the class body or a `require`.
Named arguments do not protect against later parameter renames - a rename silently breaks callers relying on the name - so treat parameter names of public constructors as API.
